A.question: Can independently checkable primal-dual Blossom certificates detect targeted tampering in the witness, graph weight, edge, matched pair or bound without accepting falsely certified optimality?
A.unit: 12 already frozen graph instances, a single verification programme, 11 predetermined attack types/instance; no fresh synthetic matching outcome
A.newness: N339 positive dual verification; N350 explicitly attacks verifier trust boundary and detects false-certification vulnerabilities.

B.strong_comparator: Unmodified N339 graph inputs and original genuine JS dual witnesses (both frozen source/result SHA); test each legitimate instance passes unchanged; deliberately invalid mutants should be rejected when applicable
B.external_oracle: Independent Python verifier was separately used in N339 and is not reused to count extra cycles; this test adversarially assesses JS production verifier
B.comparator_limit: Deterministic mutation suite, not statistical human study

C.primary: Each applicable witness tampering must throw rather than return certified; retain all ESCAPED failures as negative. Count NONAPPLICABLE separately; all 12 unmodified valid controls must verify
C.warning: Some perturbations may not invalidate optimality (eg changed edge weight by -1 but matching still optimal), thus escaping one is evidence about validator sensitivity not necessarily unsoundness; evaluate exact discrepancy, never claim fraud without mathematical counterexample.

controls: Mutation never changes N339 source files
Tampering caught by independent typed code guards
Exact result SHA checks before testing

G.epistemic: Software certificate audit only, not independent human behavior or novel theorem

H.prior: P-TRAJECTORY-INVARIANCE; NO_CHANGE_WITH_REASON even if passes, document any escape as limitation

J.count_if_real_execution: One valid technical cycle even if false negatives are found; no extra slot for each mutant
